caption: The drawing features a detailed depiction of a bird, likely an eagle, rendered in pencil or charcoal on a beige or lightly browned background. The bird is positioned in profile, facing right, with its wings extended, the left wing raised higher and more open, while the right wing is slightly lowered. The feathers on the wings, body, and tail are carefully shaded to create a realistic texture, with darker shading emphasizing the contours and structure of the bird. The eagle's beak is hooked and its mouth is slightly open, while its talons are gripping a horizontal bar or perch. The bird's head, body, and extended wings occupy most of the composition, creating a sense of motion. The drawing is bordered by a thin, rectangular line framing the image. In the lower left corner, there is a handwritten signature, "Helen Hobart." The overall color of the image is monochromatic, utilizing shades of black, gray, and off-white.
title: Weather Vane Finial
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
